extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students taking a first college course on mathematical proof / transition-to-proof
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and learning objectives for students learning to construct, write, read, and communicate mathematical proofs using standard proof techniques in a first-year college proof-oriented course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop logical thinking and abstract reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop logical thinking skills and to develop the ability to think more abstractly in a proof oriented setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on cultivating the student's capacity for formal logical reasoning and abstraction required for proof construction and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to construct and write mathematical proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the ability to construct and write mathematical proofs using standard methods of mathematical proof including direct proofs, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, case analysis, and counterexamples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction and practice in multiple proof techniques: direct proofs, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, case analysis, and use of counterexamples. Assessment likely values correct selection and rigorous execution of an appropriate proof method, clear organization, and correctness of logical steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to read and understand written mathematical proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the ability to read and understand written mathematical proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training in parsing the structure of proofs, identifying key steps and justifications, and evaluating validity and completeness of arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative thinking and problem solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop talents for creative thinking and problem solving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages inventive approaches to problems, constructing insightful examples or counterexamples, and exploring multiple solution strategies rather than rote application of procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve quality of communication in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve their quality of communication in mathematics. This includes improving writing techniques, reading comprehension, and oral communication in mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers clear mathematical exposition in writing (structure, notation, explanation), reading comprehension of mathematical text, and ability to present mathematics orally; assessments may include written proofs, explanations, and presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the nature of mathematics and its language
rubrics_metrics.description: Better understand the nature of mathematics and its language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop familiarity with mathematical terminology, symbolic notation, and conventions so students can precisely formulate statements and follow formal arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A: Guidelines for Writing Mathematical Proofs (referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix A: Guidelines for Writing Mathematical Proofs (available as a downloadable appendix to the textbook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A is a dedicated resource with concrete guidelines for writing proofs; the page references this appendix as downloadable (see book files). Specific checklist-style or stylistic rules are contained in that appendix.
